clue.text: Switch from iron measuring stick

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a rule or ruler is a stick for measuring

explanation.surface: Someone swaps an iron measuring rod for another tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb meaning change over, but it is the noun: a thin cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferule is a flat cane or rod once used to punish schoolchildren, which is what a switch is.

clue.text: Previous calculation to the advantage of Europe's top players

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: being for someone is being on their side
the opening letter of this word
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An earlier estimate favoured the best teams in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top players' suggests star athletes; 'top' only picks a letter and the players are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a calculation made beforehand of what will happen, such as the weather.

clue.text: Army unit coming from firm regularly employed by temporary ruler

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept
someone employed by a ruler is taken into their service, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a regent rules while the monarch is a minor or absent
the second and fourth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A body of troops drawn from a company that works for a caretaker ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent military unit of the army, made up of battalions or squadrons.

clue.text: Lavish praise uttered extremely loudly

indicators.note: something uttered is spoken, so the word for praise is to be heard rather than spelt
the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: to laud is to praise; in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like a word for a nobleman
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Effusive compliments shouted at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish' looks like a verb going with 'praise'; it is the adjective. The pun relies on British speech, where LAUD and LORD sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means grand and magnificent, as befits a lord, so it can describe a lavish feast or display.

clue.text: Curiously redolent of a short form of poetry

indicators.note: done curiously means done in an odd way, so the following word's letters come out strangely arranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem's short verse form oddly reminds one of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondelet is a brief French verse form of seven lines built on a refrain.

clue.text: Unoccupied work space

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

explanation.surface: An empty office or desk area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work space' looks like one phrase for an office; it splits into two printer's and musical abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or position that is open is available, not taken, which is unoccupied.

clue.text: Prevailing for a short time after assault on social worker

blocks.note: to do someone, in slang, is to beat them up
min is short for minute
ants live in colonies, the classic social insect worker

explanation.surface: A brief spell of dominance after a social worker is attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the last piece goes at the bottom. The 'social worker' is an insect, not a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominant and prevailing both mean most powerful or widespread, having the upper hand.

clue.text: Acquire a posh carriage

blocks.note: to land a job or prize is to get it
taken as written
U means upper-class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of an upper-class horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood at each end.

clue.text: Row about essentially smallish steering device

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for a row goes round the kept letters
the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the two central letters of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A rowing boat's fairly small rudder handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests rowing, which fits the steering; it means a line or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the bar fixed to a boat's rudder, used to steer it.

clue.text: Concern for doctor full of anger on reflection

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one word goes inside the other
a reflection shows things back to front, so the whole result is read in the other direction

blocks.note: Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A worried note about a physician who is seething, considered afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first; only then is the whole thing turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard and concern are synonyms for care or consideration, as in 'with no regard for others'.

clue.text: Novel in the earliest stage of development

definitions.text: in the earliest stage of development

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of an Émile Zola novel about a miners' strike

blocks.clueFragment: in the earliest stage of development
blocks.note: second meaning: an adjective for something just sprouting, like a seed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, which fits the surface; it is a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Germinal describes a seed beginning to germinate, hence anything at its very beginning; it is also Zola's 1885 novel.

clue.text: Puzzled by plot to imprison inspiring goddess

indicators.note: imprisoning something locks it inside, so the goddess goes within the plot

blocks.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground
the Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspired the arts

explanation.surface: Bewildered by a scheme to lock up a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme; it is a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered or confused, which is to be puzzled.

clue.text: Agrees with savage polemic on society

indicators.note: to savage is to maul and tear apart, so the next word's letters are torn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone endorses a fierce attack written on society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savage' reads as an adjective on 'polemic' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply is to go along with a request or rule, which is to agree to it.

clue.text: Discontent with tribune as emperor? Only some

indicators.note: only some of the words are used, so the solution is a run of letters lying within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A Roman tribune is unhappy about acting as emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: A tribune was a Roman official who protected the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of worry or dissatisfaction, a close synonym for discontent.

clue.text: Picked out from last of begonias in containers

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
plants in pots are potted

explanation.surface: A gardener chooses from among the last begonias in pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or pick it out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Go wrong at start of Easter function

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: to sin is to do wrong
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves at the beginning of an Easter celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like an event such as a party; it is a trigonometric function.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is one of the trigonometric functions, the ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse.

clue.text: Stay with American writer in South Dakota

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so the joined words go inside the state's letters

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
US is short for American
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone lodges with a US author living in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a noun for a visit; it is a verb, as in staying an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay proceedings is to halt them for a time, which is to suspend them.

clue.text: Look at cup of tea in constant agitation

blocks.note: to see is to look at
one's cup of tea is one's thing, what one likes

explanation.surface: Someone watches a cup of tea that will not stop bubbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup of tea' is the idiom for a personal favourite, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething means churning or boiling over, hence in a state of constant turmoil.

clue.text: Act as peacemaker without time to engage in contemplation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the peacemaking verb goes round the time letter

blocks.note: to mediate is to settle a dispute between others
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A peacemaker with no time to think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to engage in deep, focused thought or contemplation.

clue.text: We object after unusually pious Republican within is not genuine

indicators.note: done unusually means done in an odd manner, so the letters fall into a strange order
within means inside, so the party letter sits inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is short for Republican
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: We protest that a strangely devout Republican insider is a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' looks like a protest; grammatically it means 'we' as an object, which is US.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not what it claims to be, so not genuine.

clue.text: Note going around hospital department as a reminder

indicators.note: something going around another thing encircles it, so the department's letters sit inside the note

blocks.note: a memo is a short written note
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A memo is circulated round a hospital ward to remind staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept to remind one of a person or event.

clue.text: Went back late

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word for 'went' is read right to left

blocks.note: to go is a coy term for to urinate

explanation.surface: Someone returned home after a late night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went back late' reads as returning late; 'went' is a euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean far advanced in time, as in 'deep into the night', so it means late.

clue.text: Complete absence of friendliness following head's expression of refusal

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the friendliness phrase is placed second, behind the head's expression

blocks.note: a nod is an expression made with the head
an icy manner shows no warmth at all

explanation.surface: A cold, unfriendly shake of the head that means no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's expression of refusal' reads as one phrase, but it splits: a head's expression is the wordplay, and 'expression of refusal' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is an informal phrase meaning no or that is not going to happen, a refusal.

clue.text: Unfortunately I meant to be patient

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having intended to be tolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like the adjective meaning tolerant; it is a person in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone confined to an institution, including a patient in a hospital.

clue.text: Displaying no interest in revolt at home in London area

indicators.note: being in an area means lying inside it, so the joined words go inside its letters

blocks.note: SE is the south-east postal district of London
people who are up are in rebellion, as in 'up in arms'
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: Londoners at home can't be bothered with an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: London is divided into postal districts named by compass points, such as SE and NW.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying face up, and figuratively passive or apathetic, showing no interest or resistance.

clue.text: Talk pompously about knight being decorated

indicators.note: about means around, so the speaking verb wraps around the single letter

blocks.note: to orate is to speechify grandly
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth grandly about a knight receiving an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' suggests a knight being honoured; it means elaborately ornamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately adorned, a synonym of decorated in its sense of embellished.

clue.text: Special exercises copper gets to complain strongly about

indicators.note: turned about means turned around, so the word for complaining is read backwards

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rail is to protest bitterly

explanation.surface: A police officer on a fitness programme finds something to grumble at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal; RAIL reversed gives LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar can mean particular or special to one thing, as in 'peculiar to this region'.

clue.text: Poor in design

blocks.note: shabby or inferior
to intend or have in mind

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shoddy design; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something poor and shabby, and as a verb it means to intend or design.

clue.text: Thinks of wise men once oddly ignored in Iceland

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second and fourth of the word
being in a country places these letters inside its abbreviation

blocks.note: IS is the international code for Iceland
the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity
the even letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone pictures the old wise men being snubbed in Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like 'formerly' but only supplies letters; 'oddly ignored' drops its first and third.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form a picture of it in the mind, to think of it.

clue.text: Amazon river engulfing girl earlier? Just the opposite

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow something up, so one piece is swallowed inside the others
this flips the previous instruction, so the swallower and the swallowed swap roles

blocks.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet
ago means in the past
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A girl swept up by the Amazon river, or was it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon river' looks like one phrase but splits: Amazon is the definition. Vi is a short form of the name Violet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were legendary warrior women, so an Amazon is a fierce, domineering woman, as a virago is.

clue.text: Suddenly appearing in Spain to meet and join with conservationists

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to merge is to come together and combine
the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Something pops up in Spain as conservation groups link up.
explanation.walkthrough: The NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent describes something coming into view or existence, newly arising.

clue.text: Form of rugby just in southern Scotland at first

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken
being in something means lying inside it, so the word for fair goes between the outer letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the opening letter of this word
just and even both mean fair or level

explanation.surface: A version of rugby played only in the south of Scotland at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only' but means fair; the Melrose club in southern Scotland invented the seven-a-side game.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is rugby union played with seven players a side, a short fast version of the game.
